pr_title: Don't allow quiet or stop on embedded processes
pr_body:
- add embedded to Process
- don't allow quiet! or stop! 
- show in the Web UI as embedded 
- don't show the buttons to quiet or stop for embedded

Fixes #5714
pr_comments: @mperham Please confirm the key that goes in to `processes` is the same as `identity`? I had to update the tests to pass as it was using a different key and identity, but `Launcher` has `key = identity` - so I think this is OK
Yes, the identity is effectively the primary key for a process so that's what you'd use to look up its data in Redis.
Great, I think it's good then, unless you have any other changes in mind?

issue_context.title: Stopping embedded server from the Web UI kills the whole process
issue_context.body:
Ruby version: 2.7.5p203
Rails version: 6.0.4.8
Sidekiq / Pro / Enterprise version(s): 7.0.2

As per title - if you stop sidekiq via the Web UI stop button, the web server it is embedded in also ends.

I would expect either:
1) embedded servers don't have the option to be controlled like this - they're embedded as part of the app so it doesn't really make sense
2) sidekiq stops but the process keeps running, this would probably leave an app that depends on an embedded sidekiq in a broken state though
comments: Yeah, this falls into the category of "probably don't allow this". An embedded instance should not control the process it is running in so I'd be in favor of disabling these buttons. If you're running inside puma, you need to use puma's tools to manage the process.
Great. This is what I was also thinking. Please see PR

review_comments: these were required to have the process findable via the `ProcessSet` now
